name: Rites of the Earthmother
summary: High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof sends you across Mulgore to track down the great kodo Arra'chea. Even after the old rites, he asks his people to prove their strength, tracking, and devotion anew. Arra'chea's horn shows Cairne you are ready to serve the wider Horde.

sections.title: A Chieftain's Measure
sections.body: In Thunder Bluff, a young tauren's childhood gives way to duty. High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof asks young hunters to keep proving themselves. Reaching the high bluffs begins a life of service to the United Tauren Tribes. Cairne asks for more than a hunt for small pests: he wants proof of fieldcraft, shown by tracking and cleanly harvesting one of Mulgore's renowned wandering beasts.

sections.title: The Hunt for Arra'chea
sections.body: Arra'chea is a massive, legendary kodo whose looping path crosses the golden grasses northeast of Thunder Bluff. Bringing down this great beast takes patient stalking across the open savannah, not brute force alone. Return Arra'chea's horn to the high rise, and Cairne sends skinners and gatherers to use every part of the sacred beast for the city's provisions.

aliases: who gives rites of the earthmother
faq.answer: High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof gives you this hunt from his seat atop Thunder Bluff's high rise.
Arra'chea is a renowned kodo who wanders Mulgore's plains. His great horn proves a hunter's tracking skill and martial prowess.
Arra'chea roams a broad circular path northeast of Thunder Bluff's bluffs, circling the open plains clockwise.

faq.q: Why does Cairne ask for this hunt after I already completed the earlier rites?
faq.answer: For the tauren, earning an initial place is only the beginning of duty. Cairne asks you to keep proving your strength, humility, and hunting skill for the tribe.

faq.q: What happens to Arra'chea's body after the horn is taken?
faq.answer: Cairne sends a gathering party to retrieve Arra'chea's meat and hide. The kill feeds and clothes Thunder Bluff, as tauren tradition teaches them to honor their prey.

faq.q: Is this the same quest as the early starter rites?
faq.answer: No. The early trials in Camp Narache teach an initiate the foundational Rites of the Earthmother. This hunt in Thunder Bluff is Cairne's personal test of your continuing worth as a hunter.

angles.text: As a young shu'halo, you stand before Cairne Bloodhoof to bring him Arra'chea's horn. The rite proves your prowess honors your ancestors and Mulgore's herds.
As a hunter, you stalk a solitary, wandering behemoth across the golden plains. Tauren trackmasters pass this ancient hunting way down through generations.
As a member of the Horde, you help provide Thunder Bluff with food, leather, and materials by felling Arra'chea. The hunt reflects the shared struggle to survive that sustains the young Horde.
